paragraphs: From the mid-1960s through the 1970s, the museum and the surrounding area were partially reconstructed in accordance with the principles of Soviet urban planning. A promenade was created, connecting the museum area with Prymorskyi Boulevard; the slopes were stabilized; landscaping was improved; and new public spaces were developed. All work was carried out according to a design by the Republican Special Scientific and Restoration Production Workshops of Kyiv.

paragraphs: During the renovation, it became necessary to dismantle the courtyard outhouse located in the archway on the left, between the former carriage house (which by then had become a utility building facing Sofiivska Street) and the reading room.

The outhouse was removed, and a new facility was built adjacent to the main building on the right and connected to the city sewer system. The entrance to the new restroom was created from the small courtyard. An archway was built, and the entrance area to the former reading room was connected to the service building via a covered passageway. Thus, thanks to the creation of this much-needed additional space for the museum, three exhibition halls (Nos. 16, 17, and 18) were established.
